title: Poland's First Same-Sex Marriage Registered After Court Ruling
summary: Big news from Poland! The capital city, Warsaw, registered its first same-sex marriage on Thursday. This happened because courts said Poland must recognize same-sex marriages that were performed in other European Union (EU) countries. In November, the EU's highest court ordered Poland to do this, even though Polish law doesn't allow same-sex marriage. Then in March, Poland's highest administrative court told officials to recognize the marriage of two Polish men who got married in Germany. Warsaw's mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announced the news and promised to recognize more same-sex marriages from other EU countries. Poland's Prime Minister, Donald Tusk, apologized to same-sex couples "who, for many years, felt rejected and humiliated." He asked all Polish officials to respect everyone's dignity. But this doesn't mean Poland has to legalize same-sex marriage. Tusk's government promised to legalize civil unions (a legal status for couples that isn't marriage) for same-sex couples, but conservative politicians and the president have blocked it. For decades, LGBTQ+ people in Poland have been fighting for equal rights. This is a big step forward!
why_it_matters: This event shows that even if your country's laws are strict, international rules can push it to change, and it's a step toward making LGBTQ+ people feel accepted and safe.

background_read: Poland is a country in central Europe that joined the European Union in 2004. The EU has rules about human rights that all member countries must follow.

Same-sex marriage is legal in many EU countries, like Germany and Spain, but Poland is one of the few that still does not allow it. The EU's highest court sometimes steps in when member states treat people unfairly.
Rafał Trzaskowski is the mayor of Warsaw, the capital city of Poland. Donald Tusk is Poland's prime minister and was once the president of the European Council, a top EU position.
Article_Structure: WHO: Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski, Prime Minister Donald Tusk, same-sex couples, and the Polish administrative court.
WHAT: Warsaw officially registered its first same-sex marriage after a series of court decisions ordered Poland to honor such marriages performed in other EU countries.
WHERE: This happened in Warsaw, Poland's capital, but the court orders apply nationwide.

WHY: The EU's highest court ruled that Poland must respect marriages legally performed elsewhere in the EU, even though Polish law does not allow same-sex marriage itself. This puts pressure on Poland to treat all couples equally.

perspectives.description: Many people, including the prime minister, say this recognition gives same-sex couples the same dignity and legal protection as everyone else, ending years of feeling humiliated.
Some conservative groups in Poland believe marriage should only be between a man and a woman and worry that this change weakens their cultural and religious traditions.

Legal experts point out that Poland followed EU law, but this does not force the country to let its own citizens marry someone of the same sex inside Poland—only to respect marriages from other EU countries.
